subtitle: When the Sutlej Closed, an Empire Staggered

panels.shot: split-frame wide, left half a stormed earthwork burning over the Sutlej, right half a British general in scarlet watching a shattered pontoon bridge
panels.action: On one side Sham Singh Attariwala rides forward in white robes amid a crumbling Sikh fort at Sobraon, on the other Sir Hugh Gough stands stern on a distant ridge as the pontoon bridge on the Sutlej buckles and breaks.

dialogue.text: At Sobraon in 1846, a single broken bridge trapped an army, toppled the Khalsa, and bound the Koh-i-Noor to a foreign crown.

i18n.hi: १८४६ के सोबराओं में, एक टूटा पुल ही ने फौज फँसा दी, ख़ालसा गिर पड़ा, और कोहिनूर पर पराए ताज का दावा हो गया।

panels.shot: wide aerial establishing shot over the Sutlej river line at dawn
panels.action: The Sutlej glows under a pale winter sun; on one bank, dense Sikh entrenchments and the pontoon bridge at Sobraon, on the other, ordered British and Company lines stretching into the mist.

dialogue.text: February 1846. The Sutlej runs cold between the last strong army of an Indian kingdom and the rising power of the British Empire.

i18n.hi: फ़रवरी १८४६। सतलज की ठंडी धारा, एक ओर भारतीय रियासत की आख़िरी मज़बूत फ़ौज, दूसरी ओर उभरती ब्रिटिश ताकत।

panels.shot: dual close-up, faces mirrored, each turned slightly toward the unseen battlefield
panels.action: Sham Singh Attariwala, white-bearded and resolute, sits armored on his horse, while Hugh Gough, in worn scarlet with greying hair, peers through a telescope; both bear the hard lines of veterans.

dialogue.text: On one side rides Sham Singh Attariwala of the Khalsa, ready to die rather than retreat; on the other, Sir Hugh Gough, whose dispatches will carry this day’s tale to the London Gazette.

i18n.hi: एक तरफ़ ख़ालसा के शम सिंह अटारीवाला, पीछे हटने से बेहतर मौत को तैयार; दूसरी तरफ़ सर ह्यू गफ़, जिनकी रिपोर्ट आज का किस्सा लंदन गज़ट तक ले जाएगी।

panels.shot: slow push-in on the Sikh entrenchments and bridge works
panels.action: A broad view of the Sikh camp: earthworks facing the British, guns emplaced, behind them the long pontoon bridge arcing over the river to the far bank.

dialogue.text: Between them lies Sobraon, the Sikh bridgehead on the British bank, its entrenchments linked to the far shore by a floating bridge of boats and planks.

i18n.hi: बीच में है सोबराओं – ब्रिटिश किनारे पर सिखों का पुल-मुकाम, मिट्टी के किले, दूसरी ओर से नावों और तख़्तों के तैरते पुल से जुड़े।

panels.shot: medium shot of British officers around a campaign table
panels.action: Inside a canvas tent, British officers bend over a rough map of the Sutlej; a finger traces a bold arrow straight at the Sobraon bridgehead, while another points to where artillery will mass.

dialogue.text: Gough and Governor-General Hardinge agree: to end the First Anglo-Sikh War, the bridgehead must fall. Their letters speak of heavy risk, yet of a war they mean to finish.

i18n.hi: गफ़ और गवर्नर-जनरल हार्डिंगे का फैसला साफ़: पहला अंग्रेज़–सिख युद्ध खत्म करना है तो यह मुकाम टूटना ही होगा। ख़तों में ख़तरा भारी, इरादा और भी भारी।

panels.shot: wide shot of Sikh commanders in council inside their lines
panels.action: In a tent lined with weapons and standards, Sikh commanders sit in uneasy council; some lean forward in argument, others exchange guarded looks, a folded letter lying unopened on a low table.

dialogue.text: Within the Khalsa camp, council is divided. Lal Singh and Tej Singh command on paper, yet later correspondence and British reports alike will accuse them of sharing secrets with the enemy.

i18n.hi: ख़ालसा कैम्प के भीतर मतभेद है। कागज़ पर लाल सिंह और तेज सिंह हाकिम, पर बाद की चिट्ठियाँ और अंग्रेज़ी रिपोर्टें दोनों पर दुश्मन से राज़ बाँटने का इलज़ाम डालेंगी।

panels.shot: low-angle medium of Sham Singh mounting as distant guns glint on the horizon
panels.action: Sham Singh, in a white robe over chain mail, mounts his horse with deliberate calm as thunderclouds gather; far off, British cannon glint in the dawn light, wheels already in motion.

dialogue.speaker: sham_singh_attariwala_and_hugh_gough
dialogue.text: “Let others flee if they wish. I cross this bridge only once.”

i18n.hi: "दूसरे भागें तो भागें। मैं यह पुल दोबारा नहीं लौटूँगा।"

panels.shot: epic wide shot of the British assault beginning under smoke
panels.action: British infantry advance in long lines through morning fog, guns booming behind them; from the Sikh works, flashes of counter-fire answer as Sham Singh rides behind the trenches, rallying men.

dialogue.text: At first light on 10 February, British guns open. Gough’s own dispatch speaks of a storm of shot, of repeated assaults beaten back by the Khalsa from their earthworks.

i18n.hi: १० फ़रवरी की पहली रौशनी के साथ तोपें गरज उठती हैं। गफ़ की अपनी रिपोर्ट में बारूद का तूफ़ान, और मिट्टी के मोर्चों से ख़ालसा द्वारा हर बार धकेली गई चढ़ाइयाँ दर्ज हैं।

panels.shot: dynamic mid-range battle tableau inside Sikh entrenchments
panels.action: Within the smoke-choked trenches, Sikh soldiers fire and reload under intense pressure; Sham Singh, turbaned and serene-eyed, sits tall in the saddle amid the chaos, pointing his sword toward the enemy.

dialogue.text: Gough records heavy loss and stubborn resistance. Later Sikh tradition remembers Sham Singh riding in white, refusing to retreat, a visible pledge that he would not survive a defeated Punjab.

i18n.hi: गफ़ अपने भारी नुक़सान और ज़िद्दी मुक़ाबले को मानता है। सिख परंपरा बाद में याद रखती है सफ़ेद पोशाक में सवार शम सिंह को, जो पीछे मुड़ने से इनकार करते हैं – हारते पंजाब से पहले खुद को मिटाने की क़सम।

panels.shot: low-angle on British troops breaching with bayonets as Gough watches from the rear
panels.action: British soldiers surge up a battered earthwork, bayonets leveled, as Sikh defenders brace with matchlocks; in the rear, Gough, mounted, watches grimly, smoke swirling around him.

dialogue.text: Wave after wave, the British and Company troops press in. Gough writes of capturing the Sikh guns, of breaking into the bridgehead only after desperate, close fighting.

i18n.hi: लहर पर लहर, ब्रिटिश और कम्पनी की टुकड़ियाँ धक्का देती हैं। गफ़ लिखता है सिख तोपें हाथ आने की, और यह कि पुल-मुकाम बस जान की बाज़ी लगाकर, हाथों से हाथ की लड़ाई में ही टूटा।

panels.shot: dramatic medium shot of Sham Singh’s last charge
panels.action: Amid a tangle of broken guns and fleeing men, Sham Singh drives his horse forward toward advancing British troops, eyes steady, sword raised, white garments stark against the smoke-dark sky.

dialogue.text: In the crush, Sham Singh chooses not to fall back across the river. Sources remember him spurring into one last charge, a nobleman keeping faith with his oath more than with his commanders.

i18n.hi: उस भीड़ में, शम सिंह नदी पार लौटना नहीं चुनते। बयान कहते हैं, वे आख़िरी बार एड़ी लगाकर टूट पड़ते हैं – अपनी क़सम के सच्चे, सरदारों से ज़्यादा क़सम के वफ़ादार।

panels.shot: wide shot of the pontoon bridge under strain, packed with men and guns
panels.action: The pontoon bridge groans under a tide of retreating soldiers, carts and artillery; planks sag, boats shift, the Sutlej churning below as panicked men push forward.

dialogue.text: Behind him, the only path back is choking. The pontoon bridge heaves under the weight of retreating columns, each man fighting not the enemy, but the fear of being the last to cross.

i18n.hi: पीछे लौटने की एकमात्र राह घुट रही है। पोन्टून पुल पर भागती टुकड़ियों का बोझ, हर जवान दुश्मन से नहीं, आख़िरी पार जाने के डर से जूझ रहा है।

panels.shot: sudden dynamic wide of the bridge failing in the center
panels.action: At midspan, a section of the bridge gives way; boats yaw apart, planks tilt, men and guns tumble into the river, while those still on the bank stare in frozen horror.

dialogue.text: Then comes the moment no army can plan for. In the confusion, the bridge fails. Some later accuse treachery, others recall swollen waters and panic, but all accounts agree on the terror that follows.

i18n.hi: और फिर आता है वह पल, जिसकी कोई फ़ौज तैयारी नहीं कर सकती। अफरा-तफ़री में पुल जवाब दे देता है। किसी की नज़र में ग़द्दारी, किसी को सूजी लहरें और दहशत याद, पर हर बयान उस दहशत पर एकमत।

panels.shot: somber wide shot of the Sutlej filled with struggling figures and wreckage
panels.action: The Sutlej bears away shattered boats, floating planks, and scores of men struggling in the current; on the near bank, a few watch helplessly as comrades disappear downstream.

dialogue.text: Thousands are trapped. Some try to swim, weighed down by armor and fear; others stand where they are, fighting on until they are overrun, the river behind them as deadly as the bayonets ahead.

i18n.hi: हज़ारों फँस जाते हैं। कुछ कवच और ख़ौफ़ के बोझ के साथ तैरने कूदते हैं, कुछ वहीं जमे रहते हैं, आख़िरी साँस तक लड़ते हुए, जब तक आगे संगीनें और पीछे नदी दोनों बराबर मौत न बन जाएँ।

panels.shot: medium shot of Tej Singh’s distant figure riding away across the far bank
panels.action: On the far shore, a mounted figure identified as Tej Singh rides away from the broken bridge with his escort, his horse’s hooves throwing up sand as he looks back only once.

dialogue.text: Both British and Sikh records later accuse Tej Singh and Lal Singh of betrayal, of leaving the Khalsa to its fate while sharing movements with the British. But the bridge’s precise breaking remains disputed, half-truth and murmur.

i18n.hi: ब्रिटिश और सिख दोनों रिकार्ड बाद में तेज सिंह और लाल सिंह पर ग़द्दारी का इलज़ाम लगाएँगे – ख़ालसा को मौत पर छोड़, हरक़तें अंग्रेज़ों को बताने का। पर पुल के टूटने की ठोस घड़ी अब भी विवाद, आधा सच, आधी फुसफुसाहट।

panels.shot: low, respectful shot of the battlefield quieting after the fight
panels.action: The battlefield lies strewn with broken guns and abandoned standards; Sham Singh’s riderless horse wanders near a shattered earthwork, while in the distance Gough’s staff moves among regrouping British lines.

dialogue.text: When the smoke thins, the bridgehead is in British hands. Sham Singh Attariwala lies among his men, the Khalsa broken at Sobraon, though not shamed in the eyes of those who saw them stand.

i18n.hi: धुआँ हटते ही पुल-मुकाम अंग्रेज़ों के हाथ में है। शम सिंह अटारीवाला अपने जवानों के बीच पड़े हैं, ख़ालसा सोबराओं पर टूटा, पर देखने वालों की नज़र में बेज़ती नहीं हुई।

panels.shot: medium shot of Gough dictating his dispatch in a field tent
panels.action: Inside a canvas tent lit by a single lantern, Hugh Gough dictates to a clerk, gesturing toward the battlefield; the clerk writes quickly, sheets of paper already scattered on the table.

dialogue.text: That night, Gough shapes the battle into words: entrenched enemies, captured guns, a bridge destroyed, heavy losses. His dispatch travels to the London Gazette, fixing Sobraon in British memory.

i18n.hi: उस रात गफ़ जंग को लफ़्ज़ों में ढालता है – गढ़ों में जमे दुश्मन, क़ैद तोपें, उजड़ा पुल, भारी जाँनें। उसकी रिपोर्ट लंदन गज़ट तक जाती है, सोबराओं को ब्रिटिश याददाश्त में ठोंक देती है।

panels.shot: wide interior of the Lahore Darbar under British presence
panels.action: In the Lahore Darbar hall, young Maharaja Duleep Singh sits on a raised seat, flanked by courtiers; British officers and officials stand nearby with folded documents, their presence changing the room’s balance.

dialogue.text: Across the Sutlej, the victory reaches Lahore. The once-mighty court of Ranjit Singh now seats his young son Duleep under watchful eyes, as British power steps into the space that Sobraon opened.

i18n.hi: सतलज के पार, यह फ़तह लाहौर पहुँचती है। रणजीत सिंह का कभी गरज़ता दरबार अब उनके नन्हे बेटे दलीप को निगरानी भरी नज़रों के नीचे बैठाता है, और सोबराओं से खुली जगह में ब्रिटिश ताक़त क़दम रखती है।

panels.shot: close-up on a British and Sikh hand exchanging the Treaty of Lahore
panels.action: Two hands meet over a table: one in British uniform, one bearing Sikh rings and bangles; between them they hold the sealed parchment of the Treaty of Lahore.

dialogue.text: On 29 March 1846, the Treaty of Lahore is signed. Its clauses cut deep: territory ceded, a British resident installed, the Khalsa army reduced under foreign oversight.

i18n.hi: २९ मार्च १८४६ को लाहौर की संधि पर दस्तख़त होते हैं। शर्तें गहरी काटती हैं – ज़मीनें छोड़ी जाती हैं, एक ब्रिटिश रेज़िडेंट बैठाया जाता है, ख़ालसा फ़ौज पर परायी निगरानी में कैंची चलती है।

panels.shot: symbolic medium shot of the Koh-i-Noor being presented
panels.action: In a richly decorated chamber, a jewel casket is opened before British officials; the Koh-i-Noor diamond, set in its traditional mount, catches the light as a Sikh official looks on, expression guarded.

dialogue.text: Article 3 names a single stone. The Koh-i-Noor is ceded to Queen Victoria. A gem that had passed from Mughal to Afghan to Sikh now crosses the sea, its journey bound to Sobraon’s broken bridge.

i18n.hi: तीसरी धारा बस एक पत्थर का नाम लेती है। कोहिनूर रानी विक्टोरिया को सौंपा जाता है। मुग़ल से अफ़ग़ान से सिख हाथों से गुजरता यह हीरा अब समंदर पार जाता है, उसकी राह सोबराओं के टूटे पुल से बँध जाती है।

panels.shot: reflective wide shot over the Sutlej at dusk, empty now, with a faint ghostly suggestion of past armies
panels.action: The Sutlej flows quietly at Sobraon in dusky light, its banks empty; faint, translucent impressions of marching soldiers and a lone figure in white seem to linger over the water.

dialogue.text: Empires like the Khalsa and men like Gough and Sham Singh pass, but the river remembers the day a bridge failed, and how a kingdom’s fate turned not on advance, but on the loss of retreat.

i18n.hi: ख़ालसा जैसे साम्राज्य और गफ़, शम सिंह जैसे लोग गुज़र जाते हैं, पर नदी उस दिन को याद रखती है, जब पुल टूटा था – और जब किसी रियासत की तक़दीर हमले से नहीं, पीछे हटने की राह खोने से पलट गई थी।

subtitle_i18n.en: When the Sutlej Closed, an Empire Staggered
